title: Pop Culture Digest — Friday, November 6, 2026
description:
Thursday · November 5, 2026
Pop Culture Digest
What’s actually dominating today
Russell Brand was convicted of rape in London, the New York Times is closing in on Letterboxd, Christian Bale went eyebrow-less for Madden, and Jack Harlow dropped a new EP.
Celebrity

Russell Brand convicted of rape and three sexual assaults

After a four-week trial at Southwark Crown Court, a jury found Brand, 51, guilty Thursday of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault against four women, for offenses between 2004 and 2009 — at a radio station, on the set of a DVD recording, and at his home. He was acquitted of two other rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Bail was refused, so he spends the weekend in custody; sentencing is Monday, Nov. 9, and the judge has said he faces a significant prison term. The verdict has reopened questions about how Britain’s TV and radio industry handled complaints about him at the height of his fame.

BBC News →   ·   AP News →

Movies

The New York Times is in exclusive talks to buy Letterboxd for about $330 million

The cinephile social network — roughly 30 million users, more than half under 35 — would join Wordle, Wirecutter and The Athletic in the Times Company stable. The price is more than 20 times Letterboxd’s projected 2026 earnings of about $15 million. A24 was the last rival bidder and dropped out as the price climbed; no deal is signed yet.

Co-founders Matthew Buchanan and Karl von Randow are expected to stay in charge, and the site would likely keep running standalone while plugging into Times ad tech — which is exactly what users are nervously debating. There’s no trailer here; the links go to the coverage.

Variety →   ·   Deadline →   ·   The Verge →

Movies

Christian Bale shaved his head and plucked his eyebrows to play Al Davis in Madden

“I just shaved my head, but then the hair people went to work after that… Plucked all my eyebrows as well,” Bale told Entertainment Tonight about becoming the late Raiders owner. “I really rued the day when I had to stop playing him.”

David O. Russell’s biopic stars Nicolas Cage (in a fat suit) as John Madden, with Kathryn Hahn, Sienna Miller, John Mulaney as EA founder Trip Hawkins, and Shane Gillis. It opens in select theaters Nov. 11 and streams on Prime Video Nov. 18.

Trailer on YouTube →   ·   ComingSoon →

Music

Jack Harlow returns with the Sweet Action II EP, featuring Babyface

Harlow’s seven-track EP is out today: “SIGNORA,” “TOO SOON” with Babyface, “SHE GETS ME,” “610 MAGNOLIA,” “HOLD BACK,” “PRESSURE” and “MOVE ON.”

It lands on a stacked New Music Friday that also brings Lil Baby’s Fresh, Kings of Leon’s O My Beloved, Skepta’s The Fork and Knife and Royal Blood’s Dead Company.

Listen on Spotify →   ·   HipHop-N-More →

Bottom of the news

  • Ex–Warner Bros. film chief Pamela Abdy used her Women in Film Vanguard Award speech to say it’s “getting harder, not easier, to be a woman in the business.”
  • Ramayana: Part One (Ranbir Kapoor, Yash) opened to a reported ₹155 crore worldwide gross on day one.
  • Derek Klena takes over as Jay Gatsby in Broadway’s The Great Gatsby starting Dec. 5.
  • Shygirl’s SWALLOW!, La Roux’s first album in six years Old Flames, and Sufjan Stevens’ Worst Christmas Ever! also arrived today.
  • A24’s Jordan Firstman comedy Club Kid opens in limited release today.
